newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran and Malaysia to build up oil ties.
newsitem.headline: Iran and Malaysia to build up oil ties.

text.p: Iran and Malaysia aim to increase commercial ties in the oil industry, Iran Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh told the official Iranian news agency IRNA.
Aghazadeh, speaking to IRNA in Kuala Lumpur after a three-day visit, said Malaysia would rent an Iranian oil rig to carry out exploration work in Turkmenistan.
"The two countries also agreed to conduct joint oil explorations in southern Africa including construction of a refinery," IRNA reported at the weekend.
Malaysia had also expressed interest in developing Iran's South Pars gas field and other oil and gas fields, Aghazadeh was reported as saying.

Malaysian state oil firm Petronas has already linked up with France's Total SA to develop Iran's Sirri E and A offshore oil fields in the biggest foreign investment in Iran's energy sector since its 1979 revolution.
It is also currently part of a foreign consortium bidding for the $3.5 billion second and third phase development of Iran's huge South Pars gas field.
Iran's National Iranian Oil Company is in negotiations with two consortiums headed by Total and the Royal Dutch-Shell Group to develop the field.

U.S. President Bill Clinton signed the Iran-Libya Sanctions Act last year which gave the president powers to impose a range of sanctions against non-U.S. firms that invested $40 million or more a year in the two countries' oil and gas sectors.
Aghazadeh met Petronas president Dato Mohamed Hassan during his visit, IRNA reported.
